Alliances Caucasus 2: Regional Market Alliances for Rural Development in the SC

description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för programmet är att öka inkomsterna och förbättra försörjningsmöjligheterna för producenter på landsbygden med fokus på förbättrad och hållbar produktivitet, motståndskraftig marknadstillgång, lokala sysselsättningsmöjligheter och jämlik lokal integrering.

The overall objective of the programme is to increase income and improve livelihoods for rural producers based on improved and sustainable productivity, resilient market access, local employment opportunities and equitable inclusion locally.

The overall goal on the impact level is following:
Income increased and livelihoods improved for rural producers due to better, sustainable productivity, resilient market access, local employment opportunities and more equitable inclusion in local natural resource management and use.
Expected outcomes are as below:
1. Rural producers increase profitability and sustainability due to access to target services and inputs.
2. Sustainable and diversified MSMEs provide more reliable, value-added market access to rural producers.
3. Local institutions provide improved access to more equitable local decision making and agency over natural resource use for rural producers.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution Alliance Caucasus Program 2

description.narrative:
Improved Opportunities for Productive Employment and Decent Work - Expansion of 28 Georgian Milk Mark (GMM) dairies since May 2022 created 63 full-time job equivalents (37 female, 26 male). - 29% of jobs were filled by ethnic minorities, promoting inclusively in Azerbaijani and Armenian communities.
- Employee satisfaction is high due to critical employment opportunities in remote rural areas.
- 10 dairies formalized employment with written contracts, while others improved job security and employee benefits (e.g., 8 dairies offering paid leave). - Employee salaries increased by 5-10%, reflecting economic growth.
-A shift toward formal recruitment practices, such as advertising vacancies online, is enhancing labor market competitiveness. Strengthened Conditions for Free, Fair, and Sustainable Trade
- The Georgian Milk Mark Federation (GMMF) now includes 50 dairies serving over 13,000 small farming households.
- 28 dairies currently have permits to use the Mark, with 5 more expected to join soon.
- GMM products are increasingly available in supermarkets, supported by transparent and fair supply agreements.
- A survey of supermarket managers showed 77% prefer GMM products due to quality, reliability, and consumer demand.
Advocacy capacity of GMMF members has improved:
- 53% of members reported better ability to sell GMM products in supermarkets. - 100% felt the GMMF effectively advocates for their interests.
- 87% noted improvement in the GMMF's advocacy role over previous years.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
